title: Cornered Resource
equation: Cornered Resource Value = Asset Desirability × Exclusivity
hook: Competitors can copy your offer. They can't copy the location, the contract, or the person they don't have.
statement: Sometimes your whole advantage is one asset rivals want but simply can't get their hands on.
explainer: A patent, a prime location, an exclusive contract, a key person. If competitors want it badly and you've locked it up, that's a real moat. Its strength depends on both.
sop: List your assets: talent, IP, locations, contracts, data, relationships.
Rate Asset Desirability from 1 to 10 for each.
Rate Exclusivity from 1 to 10 for each.
Lock in the strongest one with contracts or relationships.
Don't bet the business on anything that's only exclusive for now.
equation_example: Asset Desirability 9 × Exclusivity 8 = 72. High on both means a lasting edge. A great asset you haven't locked up, 9 × 2 = 18, is something rivals will soon have too.
question: Name one asset you have that a competitor would want but couldn't buy.
closing_statement: Real advantage is what others want and can't just buy.
caption:
Principle Nº 347: Cornered Resource

Competitors can copy your offer. They can't copy the location, the contract, or the person they don't have.

Sometimes your whole advantage is one asset rivals want but simply can't get their hands on.
